title: Design System: WikiHunt — The Departure Board

display.purpose: Uppercase headings, origin/target titles, section labels.

flap.purpose: Exclusively inside .flap-cell: the timer and the room code. Never running text.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy, form fields, table cells.

label.purpose: Uppercase small caps for stat labels, badges, field labels. 11px floor.

shadows.name: panel-lip
shadows.purpose: Cards, sidebar, article pane, toasts — a physical bezel's lip.

shadows.name: recessed-cell
shadows.purpose: Inputs, flap cells, code chips — a character sunk into the board.

motion.name: flap-flip
motion.purpose: A flap cell's character-change flip: compress toward zero, swap the character at the midpoint, release.

motion.name: ease-timer
motion.purpose: Timer-bar transform:scaleX transition; background swaps to the delayed/urgent color over 0.3s ease.

components.name: Flap Display
components.description: The signature component: any glance-read number (timer, room code) renders as a row of physical flap cells with a visible seam, flipping only the characters that change.
components.css: .flap-row { display: inline-flex; gap: 3px; } .flap-cell { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 0.85em; background: #0a0a0c; border: 1px solid #303036; border-radius: 2px; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.6); font-family: 'Big Shoulders Stencil Display', monospace; font-weight: 700; font-size: 22px; padding: 4px 6px; color: #eae6da; overflow: hidden; transition: transform 0.09s ease-in; } .flap-cell::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 50%; height: 1px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.7); } .flap-cell.urgent { color: #f35f5f; } .flap-cell.flipping { transform: scaleY(0.05); }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary call to action.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; font-family: 'Archivo', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; padding: 12px 20px; border-radius: 2px; border: 1px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.08s ease, background 0.12s ease; } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary { background: #ffb020; color: #1a1200; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #ffc04d; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Recessed board-black cell, standard across every form.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #0a0a0c; border: 1px solid #303036; color: #eae6da; padding: 11px 14px; border-radius: 2px; font-size: 15px; font-family: 'Archivo', sans-serif; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.6); outline: none; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #d98c00; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.6), 0 0 0 3px rgba(255,176,32,0.2); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #8d8f98; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat gunmetal panel with a hard panel-lip shadow, no gradient, no border-radius softness beyond 6px.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #18181c; border: 1px solid #303036; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.9), 0 3px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.5), 0 3px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.35); padding: 28px; color: #eae6da; }

components.name: Difficulty Badge
components.description: Board-black tag with a colored left flag border standing in for a physical status flag — no pill, no tinted fill.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 3px 9px 3px 8px; border-radius: 2px; border-left: 3px solid currentColor; background: #0a0a0c; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; } .ds-badge-medium { color: #ffb020; }

components.name: Player Chip
components.description: A player's live status: a square LED plus an uppercase status word, reused in host view, sidebar, and roster.
components.css: .ds-chip { padding: 7px 12px; border-radius: 2px; background: #212126; border: 1px solid #303036; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; color: #eae6da; font-family: 'Archivo', sans-serif; } .ds-led { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 1px; display: inline-block; } .ds-led-near { background: #ffb020; box-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(255,176,32,0.7); } .ds-status { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: #ffb020; }

components.name: Breadcrumb Stub
components.description: A visited article as a clickable ticket-stub-styled button; the current position is the non-interactive amber-highlighted stub at the end.
components.html: ›Gato
components.css: .ds-breadcrumb { display: flex; gap: 6px; align-items: center; font-size: 12.5px; color: #8d8f98; } .ds-crumb { padding: 3px 10px; border-radius: 2px; background: #18181c; border: 1px solid #303036; border-bottom: 2px dashed #303036; font: inherit; color: inherit; } .ds-crumb-link { cursor: pointer; } .ds-crumb-link:hover { background: #212126; border-color: #d98c00; color: #eae6da; } .ds-crumb-current { color: #ffb020; border-color: #d98c00; border-bottom-style: solid; } .ds-sep { opacity: 0.5; }

narrative.overview:
WikiHunt reads as a mechanical split-flap board at a terminal gate — the kind that once hung in every airport and train station, its characters flipping into place with an audible click. The product's own mechanism (racing from a shared origin article to a shared target through nothing but real links) maps directly onto that world's own grammar: a board that always shows FROM and TO, a clock that counts down in physical digits, and a status column that reads DEPARTED / EN ROUTE / BOARDING instead of drawing on the visitor's imagination.

This direction was assigned by a dice roll against six catalog challengers, fused and weighed on audience identification and product clarity. None beat it outright; two — an oscilloscope's live-signal legibility and a guide-map's warm sense of journey — were strong enough to raise it. The physical scene forced the palette: someone glances at this from across a couch at a game night, the way you'd glance up at an actual departure board — so it reads dark not because dark is a template default, but because terminal boards are dark, lit from within.
keyCharacteristics: Board black and gunmetal neutrals with exactly one accent — amber.
Numbers a player must read under pressure render as physical flap cells with a real flip transition, not plain digits.
Corners are almost square — no soft, pill-shaped chrome anywhere.
Depth comes from a recessed-cell inset shadow and a hard-edged panel lip, never a soft ambient glow.
Status is read as a word backed by a small square LED, not inferred from a colored dot alone.
The Wikipedia article pane stays its authentic light-mode self at rest — the one deliberate exception to the board's otherwise all-dark world.

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: Amber is the system's only accent color. It never shares a component with a second saturated hue; the status vocabulary (blue/green/red) is locked to player/room state and never used decoratively.

rules.name: The Flap-for-Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any number a player must read under time pressure — the timer, a room code, a score — renders through the Flap Display component, not as plain text.

rules.name: The Recessed-or-Lipped Rule
rules.body: A surface is either a raised panel (Panel Lip shadow) or a recessed cell (Recessed Cell shadow) — never a soft ambient glow, and never both on the same element.

dos: Do render any glance-read number through the Flap Display component — never as plain display-face text.
Do keep Amber Glow as the system's only accent; the status vocabulary is locked to player/room state, never decorative.
Do give status its own word (A CAMINHO / EMBARQUE / PARTIU), not just a colored LED.
Do keep every surface either a raised panel or a recessed cell, never a soft ambient glow.
Do keep the article reading pane in its authentic light-mode Wikipedia styling at rest.
donts: Don't round a corner past 6px — this board has no pill-shaped chrome anywhere.
Don't introduce a text color below 4.5:1 contrast against any of the three neutral surfaces.
Don't set functional UI text below 11px — the label floor.
Don't reach for a soft ambient drop shadow; depth comes from the Panel Lip or Recessed Cell treatments only.
Don't restyle the article pane toward a casual mobile-app look.
